upper_bound.quote: This is a common-refinement (overlay) construction: superimpose the concatenated intervals of $B$ on an initial segment of length $q$ of the concatenated intervals of $A$, cut both rows at the union of the division points and pair the corresponding cells; the bound on the number of cuts follows by counting the cells of the common refinement (standard; details omitted).
upper_bound.witness: The missing statement is a proof, for arbitrary disjoint nonempty collections A and B, that this overlay can be implemented using at most |A|+|B|-1 legal new cuts while pairing all length q and leaving exactly p-q unpaired. The passage sketches the construction but explicitly omits the cut count, so it does not establish the required all-cases lemma.
upper_bound.load_bearing: The upper bound's final cut budget in (13) directly uses this unproved |A|+|B|-1 estimate. Without it, the text has not shown that Xiang's proposed response always uses at most n marks.

parsed.notes: The stated closed form is correct. The reduction and powers-of-two lower bound are complete; the upper bound depends on an explicitly omitted proof of the crucial overlay cut count.
